headline: Light rain and snow showers end around midnight tonight, Monday into Tuesday is the best window for holiday travel over the Sierra, a weaker storm brings mountain snow and strong ridge winds Tuesday night into Wednesday, and Thanksgiving looks dry and mild.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A passing weather system brings periods of snow showers through this evening, with rain mixed in at valley levels this afternoon, and showers fade completely around midnight. Around Mammoth Lakes, chances are low, about 10 to 20 percent for light snow showers between about 4 and 10 PM; the best chances (30 to 60 percent) are along I-80, with 15 to 30 percent along the Sierra crest. Snow totals stay light: up to about 2 inches at the Sierra crest (20 to 30 percent chance of more than 2 inches by Monday morning), a trace to an inch elsewhere in the Sierra and foothills, and little to none in the Reno-Sparks area, where the snow level near 5,500 feet means mostly rain or a rain-snow mix. Freezing fog may form in eastern Sierra valleys such as Truckee and Tahoe overnight into late Monday morning, so use caution traveling on fog-reduced and recently snowy roads.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: High pressure brings dry weather Monday into early Tuesday, the safest travel window for anyone crossing the Sierra for the holiday. Another, weaker storm arrives late Tuesday into Wednesday with snow returning to northeast California and the Sierra through Wednesday afternoon; it keeps trending drier, with a 20 to 60 percent chance of 2 or more inches at the Sierra crest and a 30 to 50 percent chance of an inch or more on the Sierra passes by Wednesday evening. Snow levels start around 5,000 to 5,500 feet Tuesday night and rise to about 6,000 to 6,500 feet by late Wednesday afternoon, so any valley showers would fall as rain, and showers spilling into the western Nevada valleys look limited (15 to 25 percent chance). Sierra ridge gusts could reach 60 to 70 mph Tuesday night, so check for updates if you must cross the Sierra late Tuesday into Wednesday.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: High pressure builds back in behind the midweek storm, bringing warmer and drier weather for Thanksgiving Day and Friday. Longer-range computer models keep hinting at a wetter and windier storm the following weekend, but the details are uncertain this far out.

watch_for: Freezing fog in eastern Sierra valleys tonight into Monday morning, on top of slick roads from recent snow.
Tuesday night into Wednesday: light Sierra snow on the passes and ridge gusts of 60 to 70 mph during busy holiday travel.
A possibly wetter and windier storm next weekend.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in light snow tonight and a dry Monday into Tuesday, note the midweek storm keeps trending drier, and say next weekend's storm is still uncertain.
